topic: How small is an atom?
hook: Look at your fingertip. Now zoom in a hundred million times.
payoff: Only at ×100 million do you reach a single atom.
numbers: fingertip 1.6 cm; skin cell 30 µm; DNA 2.5 nm wide; atom ~0.3 nm
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: How far away is the Moon, really?
hook: The Moon looks close… but it isn't.
payoff: Every other planet lined up almost exactly fills the gap.
numbers: Earth–Moon avg 384,400 km; 7 planets' diameters sum ≈380,000 km
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: How long is your DNA unwound?
hook: Your DNA is coiled inside a nucleus 0.006 mm wide.
payoff: Stretched out, one cell's DNA is about 2 m — taller than you.
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: How big is the biggest star?
hook: This is our Sun. Now meet UY Scuti.
payoff: Put it in the Sun's place and it swallows Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: What if Earth stopped spinning?
hook: The ground under you moves at 1,670 km/h.
payoff: If Earth stopped, the air wouldn't — winds faster than a jet.
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: If the Sun were a basketball, where would Earth be?
hook: Shrink the Sun to a basketball.
payoff: Earth is a 2 mm pinhead 26 m away — a whole court.
numbers: Sun 24 cm → Earth 2.2 mm at 26 m
note: 10 s test sample exists; make the full 30 s version

topic: How many Earths fit inside the Sun?
hook: Fill the Sun with Earths. How many?
payoff: About 1.3 million.
numbers: Sun volume ≈1.3 million Earths; 109 Earths across

topic: How big is Jupiter compared to Earth?
hook: Earth feels huge. Put it next to Jupiter.
payoff: 11 Earths fit across Jupiter, about 1,300 inside it.
numbers: Jupiter 139,820 km vs Earth 12,742 km; volume ≈1,321×

topic: How old is the sunlight you see?
hook: The sunlight on your face isn't new.
payoff: It left the Sun 8 minutes 20 seconds ago.
numbers: 1 AU = 149.6 million km; light 299,792 km/s → 499 s

topic: If the Sun were a basketball, where is the nearest star?
hook: Our Sun is a basketball. Where is the next one?
payoff: About 7,000 km away — another continent.

topic: How thin is Earth's atmosphere?
hook: All the air you'll ever breathe is in one thin layer.
payoff: On a 20 cm globe it would be thinner than 2 mm.
numbers: Kármán line 100 km vs Earth 12,742 km

topic: How deep is the deepest ocean?
hook: Drop Mount Everest into the Mariana Trench.
payoff: Its peak would still be about 2 km underwater.

topic: How deep have humans ever dug?
hook: The deepest hole ever drilled is over 12 km deep.
payoff: That's only 0.2% of the way to Earth's centre.
numbers: Kola Superdeep 12,262 m; Earth radius 6,371 km

topic: How many cells are in your body?
hook: You are not one thing. You're a crowd.
payoff: About 30 trillion human cells — 3,750× the people on Earth.
numbers: ~30 trillion cells (Sender et al. 2016); ~8 billion people

topic: How small is a virus?
hook: A grain of sand looks tiny. Zoom into it.
payoff: A typical virus is ~100 nm — 10,000 fit across a sand grain.
numbers: sand ~1 mm; bacterium ~1-2 µm; virus ~100 nm

topic: How tall is Olympus Mons?
hook: The tallest mountain isn't on Earth.
payoff: Olympus Mons on Mars is about 2.5 Everests tall.

topic: How high is the space station, really?
hook: The space station feels far away.
payoff: If Earth were a basketball, the ISS would fly 7 mm above it.

topic: How fast does the space station go?
hook: The ISS is moving at 28,000 km/h right now.
payoff: Astronauts see about 16 sunrises every day.

topic: How thin are Saturn's rings?
hook: Saturn's rings are wider than 20 Earths.
payoff: But they're often only about 10 m thick.
numbers: main rings ~280,000 km wide; ~10 m to 1 km thick

topic: How big is the Milky Way?
hook: Shrink the whole Solar System to the size of a coin.
payoff: The Milky Way would still be ~2,500 km wide.
numbers: MW ~100,000 ly; Neptune orbit ~60 AU across

topic: How fast is Earth moving around the Sun?
hook: You're sitting still… or are you?
payoff: Earth carries you at about 107,000 km/h.

topic: How fast is light?
hook: Light could circle Earth in a blink.
payoff: 7.5 times around Earth every second.

topic: How far does light go in a nanosecond?
hook: Light is the fastest thing there is.
payoff: In one nanosecond it travels about 30 cm — a ruler.

topic: How heavy is a neutron star?
hook: This star is only about 20 km wide.
payoff: A teaspoon of it would weigh about a billion tonnes.

topic: How small would Earth be as a black hole?
hook: Crush the whole Earth into a black hole.
payoff: It would be under 2 cm wide — a marble.

topic: How small would the Sun be as a black hole?
hook: Squeeze the Sun until it becomes a black hole.
payoff: It would be only about 6 km wide — a small town.

topic: How big is Pluto, really?
hook: Pluto was once called a planet.
payoff: It's smaller than our Moon — narrower than the USA.
numbers: Pluto 2,377 km; Moon 3,474 km; USA ~4,500 km

topic: How big is the Moon, really?
hook: Put the Moon down on Earth's map.
payoff: It's almost as wide as Australia.

topic: How long is a light-year?
hook: A light-year sounds like time. It's a distance.
payoff: About 9.46 trillion km.

topic: How far can you see to the horizon?
hook: Stand on a beach and look out to sea.
payoff: The horizon is only about 5 km away.

topic: How big is a blue whale?
hook: The biggest animal that ever lived is alive today.
payoff: A blue whale is about as long as a basketball court.

topic: How tall is the tallest tree?
hook: The tallest living tree is hidden in California.
payoff: Hyperion is 116 m — taller than the Statue of Liberty.
numbers: Hyperion ~116 m; Statue of Liberty 93 m incl. pedestal

topic: How big is the inside of an atom?
hook: Atoms feel solid. They're mostly empty.
payoff: If the nucleus were a blueberry, the atom would be ~600 m wide.
numbers: hydrogen: atom ~1e-10 m vs proton ~1.7e-15 m (~60,000×)

topic: How thick is a human hair?
hook: A hair looks thin. Zoom in.
payoff: About 0.07 mm — just 9 red blood cells side by side.
numbers: hair ~70 µm; red blood cell ~7.5 µm

topic: How many Earths fit between Earth and the Sun?
hook: Line up Earths between us and the Sun.
payoff: You'd need about 11,700 of them.

topic: How many Earths fit across the Sun?
hook: Line up Earths across the Sun's face.
payoff: 109 of them, edge to edge.

topic: How big was the dinosaur-killing asteroid?
hook: It was about 10 km wide.
payoff: Set down on Earth, it would stand taller than Everest.

topic: How far away is Voyager 1?
hook: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and never stopped.
payoff: It's so far that its signal takes about a day to reach us.
numbers: ~25 billion km; light ~23 h (check current value)

topic: How big is the biggest black hole?
hook: This black hole weighs 66 billion Suns.
payoff: It could fit dozens of Solar Systems inside it.
numbers: TON 618 ~66e9 M☉; radius ~1,300 AU vs Neptune 30 AU

topic: How high do planes fly?
hook: Planes cruise about 11 km up.
payoff: That's the same as the depth of the deepest ocean.

topic: How big is the Pacific Ocean?
hook: Take every continent on Earth.
payoff: They'd all fit inside the Pacific — with room to spare.
numbers: Pacific ~165 million km²; land ~149 million km²

topic: How much water is on Earth?
hook: Earth looks like a water planet.
payoff: All its water would make a ball only ~1,400 km wide.

topic: How long is a day on Venus?
hook: A day on Venus lasts longer than its year.
payoff: One spin takes 243 Earth days; one orbit 225.

topic: How long would it take to drive to the Moon?
hook: Could you drive to the Moon?
payoff: At 100 km/h, nonstop, about 160 days.

topic: How long would it take to drive to the Sun?
hook: Now drive to the Sun.
payoff: At 100 km/h it would take about 170 years.

topic: How long would it take to walk around Earth?
hook: Walk around the equator without stopping.
payoff: About 334 days — almost a year.

topic: How long to fall through the Earth?
hook: Dig a tunnel straight through the Earth and jump.
payoff: You'd pop out the other side in about 42 minutes.

topic: How big is Earth's core?
hook: Deep under your feet is a ball of metal.
payoff: The inner core is about 70% as wide as the Moon.
numbers: inner core ~2,440 km wide; Moon 3,474 km

topic: How many Moons fit inside Earth?
hook: The Moon looks big in the sky.
payoff: About 50 Moons would fit inside Earth.

topic: How big is Mercury?
hook: Mercury is a planet. The Moon isn't.
payoff: Yet Mercury is only about 40% wider than the Moon.

topic: How many neurons are in your brain?
hook: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons.
payoff: That's more than 10 for every person on Earth.

topic: How big is a red blood cell?
hook: You have about 25 trillion red blood cells.
payoff: Each one is only ~0.0075 mm wide — 130 across a pinhead.

topic: How small is a tardigrade?
hook: The toughest animal on Earth is barely visible.
payoff: A tardigrade is about half a millimetre long.

topic: How big is the biggest hailstone?
hook: Hail is usually pea-sized.
payoff: The record US hailstone was 20 cm across — a volleyball.

topic: How big is the Grand Canyon?
hook: The Grand Canyon is 446 km long.
payoff: And up to 1.8 km deep — over four Empire State Buildings.
numbers: 446 km long; ~1.8 km deep; ESB 443 m

topic: How tall is Mount Everest compared to Earth?
hook: Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.
payoff: On a basketball-sized Earth it would be 0.2 mm high.

topic: How far away is Mars?
hook: Mars is our neighbour.
payoff: Even at its closest, it's about 140 times farther than the Moon.

topic: How big is the Sun in the sky vs your thumb?
hook: Hold your thumb out at arm's length.
payoff: Your thumbnail can hide the whole Sun — and the Moon.

topic: How big is the Andromeda galaxy in our sky?
hook: There's a galaxy in our sky bigger than the Moon.
payoff: Andromeda is about 6 Moons wide — just too faint to see.

topic: How big is Betelgeuse?
hook: Betelgeuse is the red star in Orion's shoulder.
payoff: In the Sun's place it would reach past Mars.

topic: How big is the Earth's shadow?
hook: Every lunar eclipse shows you Earth's shadow.
payoff: The shadow on the Moon is about 2.6 Moons wide.

topic: How long is the equator?
hook: Walk the whole equator.
payoff: 40,075 km — driving nonstop at 100 km/h takes about 17 days.

topic: How big is a grain of sand?
hook: A grain of sand is tiny.
payoff: But it holds roughly 40 quintillion atoms.
numbers: 1 mm quartz grain ≈ 1.4 mg SiO2 ≈ 4e19 atoms (order of magnitude)

topic: How far away is the edge of the observable universe?
hook: You can only see so far into space.
payoff: About 46 billion light-years in every direction.

topic: How many stars are in the Milky Way?
hook: Count every star in our galaxy.
payoff: Around 100 to 400 billion.

topic: How big is Ganymede?
hook: The biggest moon in the Solar System is a giant.
payoff: Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury.

topic: How small is a bacterium?
hook: Your hands are covered in life you can't see.
payoff: A typical bacterium is 1–2 µm — about 500 fit across a pinhead.
